issue.title: Agent Clan glossary strand says members run in parallel; 87% of clans are %wait-layered

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
The first sentence defines an agent clan as "a named, rootless container for agents that
run in parallel." That is inaccurate for most clans. Layering the declared intra-clan
`%wait` edges of every 2026 clan generation recorded on athena (1,241 generations,
10,188 member-turn `agent_meta.json` files) gives two or more dependency layers for
1,082 of them (87%):

- epic clans: 732 of 742;
- research swarms: 177 of 182;
- `toobig-` chains: 171 of 311.

Epic phases `%w` their blockers, and `.land` waits on every phase. A research swarm's
`.final` waits on the researchers, and `.linker` waits on `.final` and any media agents.

Proposed wording: "An agent clan is a named, rootless container for related agents,
which run in parallel unless `%wait` orders them into dependency layers." Keep the rest
of the strand.

If the clan-waves feature from the research report ships, also add a **Clan Wave**
term: a dependency layer of one clan generation's direct members, derived from declared
`%wait` edges, distinct from queue admission. Leave that addition to the
implementation.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching clan-wave visualization: the Agent Clan glossary strand still says members run in parallel, but measured clan data shows 87% of clans are dependency-ordered, so agents relying on the definition get the wrong mental model.
